name: Idli
subtitle: Steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal, the lightest thing in Indian breakfast
prepNotes: The urad dal is ground first and separately, with cold water, until it is light and holds a peak. That aeration is what makes idlis fluffy — the fermentation only builds on it.
Idli batter is thicker than dosa batter. If it pours easily it is too thin.

steps.text: Soak the rice in one bowl and the urad dal with fenugreek in another, for 5 hours. Soak the poha for 20 minutes before grinding.
Grind the urad dal first with cold water until white, fluffy and doubled in volume. Test it: a spoon of batter should float in water.
steps.tip: This is the single most important step. Do not rush or overheat it.

steps.text: Grind the rice to a slightly grainy paste, then fold the two together by hand with salt.
steps.tip: By hand — the warmth helps fermentation start.

steps.text: Cover loosely and ferment 8-12 hours until risen and bubbly.
Grease the idli plates, fill three-quarters full, and steam 10-12 minutes. A skewer should come out clean.
steps.tip: Do not oversteam; idlis turn dense and wet.

steps.text: Rest 3 minutes before unmoulding, then serve with sambar and coconut chutney.

storage: Batter keeps 4 days refrigerated, growing more sour. Cooked idlis keep a day and steam back to life in 3 minutes; they are also the basis of idli upma.
